blocks.prompt: 1. Find equation of the altitude of triangle \(XYZ\) from vertex \(X(1, 3)\), \(Y(5, 7)\) and \(Z(-3, 9)\).
blocks.explanation:
The vertices are \(X(1, 3)\), \(Y(5, 7)\), \(Z(-3, 9)\); we need the altitude drawn from \(X\).
An altitude passes through its vertex and is perpendicular to the opposite side, here \(YZ\).
Plan: slope of \(YZ\), then the perpendicular slope (\(m_1m_2 = -1\)), then point-slope form through \(X\).
steps:
Given: \(X(1, 3)\), \(Y(5, 7)\), \(Z(-3, 9)\).
To find: the altitude from \(X\).
Method: the altitude from \(X\) is perpendicular to \(\overline{YZ}\) and passes through \(X\); use point-slope form.

Slope of \(\overline{YZ}\)
\[m_{YZ} = \dfrac{9 - 7}{-3 - 5} = \dfrac{2}{-8} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\]
Why: slope \(= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\) for the two ends of the side.

Slope of the altitude
\[m = \dfrac{-1}{m_{YZ}} = \dfrac{-1}{-\frac{1}{4}} = 4\]
Why: perpendicular lines have \(m_1m_2 = -1\), so the slope is the negative reciprocal.

Equation through \(X(1, 3)\)
\[y - 3 = 4(x - 1)\]
\[y - 3 = 4x - 4\]
\[4x - y - 1 = 0\]
Why: point-slope form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\), then bring all terms to one side.

Check:
\(X(1, 3)\): \(4 - 3 - 1 = 0\). Slope of the line is \(4\) and \(4 \times \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = -1\), so it is perpendicular to \(YZ\).
